events.title: Astronomers Begin Planning a Wide-Field Survey Telescope
events.detail: In the early-to-mid 1990s, a group of astronomers led by Tony Tyson and collaborators began planning a large-aperture, wide-field telescope capable of imaging the entire visible sky every few nights — an idea that would eventually become the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST).

events.title: NSF and DOE Begin Backing the Large-Aperture Synoptic Survey Telescope
events.detail: Between 2001 and 2010 the Large-Aperture Synoptic Survey Telescope (LSST) received formal support from the National Science Foundation and the U.S. Department of Energy, alongside a $30 million private pledge from software billionaires Charles Simonyi and Bill Gates.

events.title: Stanford and SLAC Launch KIPAC, Anchoring LSST's Physics Partnership
events.detail: Stanford University and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory jointly launched the Kavli Institute for Particle Astrophysics and Cosmology (KIPAC), setting in motion the DOE-side physics collaboration that would eventually build the LSST Camera.

events.title: Charles Simonyi Fund Gives $20 Million for Telescope Mirrors
events.detail: The Charles Simonyi Fund for Arts and Sciences provided a $20 million gift that enabled fabrication of the telescope's unique three-mirror optical system, later recognized when the telescope was named the Simonyi Survey Telescope.

events.title: National Academies Decadal Survey Ranks LSST the Top Ground-Based Priority
events.detail: The National Academies' 2010 astronomy and astrophysics decadal survey, 'New Worlds, New Horizons,' ranked LSST as the highest-priority large ground-based project for the decade, cementing the funding case for NSF and DOE construction support.

events.title: NSF Formally Authorizes Construction
events.detail: NSF formally authorized construction of the observatory in August 2014, launching a project originally planned to run 99 months, with Cerro Pachón in Chile selected as the summit site.

events.title: 'First Stone' Ceremony Marks Start of Summit Construction
events.detail: On April 14, 2015, Chilean President Michelle Bachelet, then-NSF Director France Córdova, LSST Director Steven Kahn, U.S. Ambassador Michael A. Hammer, and donor Charles Simonyi unveiled the traditional 'First Stone' (Primera Piedra) at Cerro Pachón, marking the formal start of summit construction.

events.title: Telescope Mount and Mirror Components Begin Arriving On-Site
events.detail: The telescope's mount structure and mirror components began arriving at the Cerro Pachón summit facility, as dome and support-building construction progressed in parallel.

events.title: Congress Renames the Observatory for Astronomer Vera C. Rubin
events.detail: An act of the U.S. Congress, enacted December 20, 2019 after a proposal by Rep. Eddie Bernice Johnson and Rep. Jenniffer González-Colón, renamed the Large Synoptic Survey Telescope the NSF Vera C. Rubin Observatory — the first U.S. national observatory named for a woman, honoring the astronomer whose rotation-curve measurements provided some of the first strong evidence for dark matter.

events.title: LSST Camera Construction Completed at SLAC
events.detail: After two decades of work, the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory team completed construction of the 3,200-megapixel LSST Camera — the largest camera ever built for astronomy — ahead of shipment to Chile.

events.title: LSST Camera Arrives at Cerro Pachón
events.detail: The car-sized LSST Camera arrived at the Rubin Observatory summit on May 16, 2024, after being shipped from California in a custom frame wrapped in electrostatic-discharge protection.

events.title: Simonyi Survey Telescope Dedicated in Summit Ceremony
events.detail: NSF and DOE formally named and dedicated the observatory's 8.4-meter telescope the Simonyi Survey Telescope on October 4, 2024, at a Cerro Pachón ceremony attended by the Simonyi family and Rubin Observatory, NSF, DOE, and NOIRLab leadership.

events.title: Telescope Captures 'First Photon' with Commissioning Camera
events.detail: With all three mirrors and the engineering Commissioning Camera (ComCam) installed, the fully integrated Simonyi Survey Telescope captured its first night-sky images on October 24, 2024, beginning the on-sky commissioning campaign.

events.title: LSST Camera Installed on the Simonyi Survey Telescope
events.detail: In early March 2025 the Rubin Observatory team lifted the 3,200-megapixel LSST Camera into position on the Simonyi Survey Telescope on Cerro Pachón, the final major hardware milestone before on-sky commissioning with the full science camera.

events.title: 'First Look' Commissioning Finds Over 1,500 New Asteroids
events.detail: During First Look commissioning observations in April and May 2025, the LSST Camera detected 1,514 previously unknown asteroids, following 73 found in earlier engineering tests with the Commissioning Camera in late 2024.

events.title: Rubin Observatory Unveils First Images to the Public
events.detail: At a June 23, 2025 press event in Washington, D.C. ('Rubin First Look'), NSF and DOE unveiled the observatory's first public images, including a view of the Virgo Cluster spanning a field of view 45 times the area of the full moon, alongside thousands of newly detected asteroids from just 10 hours of observation.

events.title: Data Preview 1 (DP1) Released to Data Rights Holders
events.detail: Rubin released Data Preview 1 on June 30, 2025 — 1,792 science-grade exposures from 48 commissioning nights covering seven fields in six photometric bands (ugrizy), totaling roughly 3.5 TB and about 2.3 million cataloged astrophysical objects, including 431 solar system objects (93 newly discovered).

events.title: Rubin Recovers Precovery Images of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS
events.detail: After the ATLAS survey discovered interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS (C/2025 N1) on July 1, 2025, astronomers found the object hiding in Rubin commissioning data going back to June 21 — ten days before its official discovery — providing some of the earliest large-telescope measurements of its astrometry, photometry, and activity.

events.title: Early Optimization Surveys Turn Up 380 Trans-Neptunian Objects
events.detail: During Rubin's early optimization surveys in summer 2025, astronomers identified roughly 380 trans-Neptunian objects, including two — provisionally designated 2025 LS2 and 2025 MX348 — on extremely elongated orbits reaching about 1,000 times Earth's distance from the Sun, among the 30 most distant minor planets known.

events.title: Chile Observatories Form Dark Skies Council
events.detail: Rubin Observatory joined ESO, Gemini, and other international observatories operating in Chile to launch a Dark Skies Council coordinating light-pollution and satellite-brightness mitigation to protect the country's night skies.

events.title: Proposed FY2026 NSF Budget Cuts Raise Concerns Despite Rubin Carve-Out
events.detail: The administration's FY2026 budget proposal cut the overall NSF budget by more than half, but explicitly shielded Rubin Observatory operations with $32 million requested — still about 20% below the funding level the American Astronomical Society says was previously projected for the start of science operations.

events.title: 3I/ATLAS Sparks Public Debate Over Natural vs. Artificial Origin
events.detail: Interstellar object 3I/ATLAS became the subject of wide public debate after Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb cited unusual orbital and compositional anomalies to argue a technological origin could not be ruled out (estimating roughly 30–40% likelihood), a position most astronomers — citing Rubin and other telescope data consistent with a natural comet — have pushed back against.

events.title: Satellite Megaconstellations Threaten Rubin's Wide-Field Science
events.detail: Astronomers warned that planned low-Earth-orbit satellite megaconstellations — potentially numbering over a million objects versus tens of thousands tracked today — could brighten the night sky up to threefold and cause Rubin to miss roughly 15% of hazardous near-Earth asteroids in affected images, prompting new scheduling and image-processing mitigation research.

events.title: Pre-Survey Observations Spot Fastest-Spinning Large Asteroid on Record
events.detail: Rubin pre-survey observations identified asteroid 2025 MN45, which completes one rotation roughly every 1.88 minutes — the shortest known rotation period of any asteroid larger than 0.5 km in diameter.

events.title: Data Preview 1 Updated with Refined Calibrations
events.detail: Rubin issued an updated version of Data Preview 1 on January 8, 2026, refining calibrations and data-quality flags ahead of the transition to full science operations.

events.title: Rubin Launches Real-Time Alert Stream for the Global Astronomy Community
events.detail: Rubin Observatory activated its real-time alert stream — up to roughly 10 million alerts and 10 TB of difference-imaging data per night — distributed to a set of community alert brokers for classification and follow-up by astronomers worldwide.

events.title: Early Survey Data Reveals Over 11,000 New Asteroids
events.detail: NSF–DOE Rubin Observatory announced that preliminary data from its early optimization surveys had revealed more than 11,000 new asteroids — confirmed by the IAU Minor Planet Center — the largest single batch of asteroid discoveries submitted in the prior year, which scientists called just 'the tip of the iceberg.'

events.title: Legacy Survey of Space and Time Officially Begins
events.detail: After commissioning checkouts ran longer than the initially anticipated early-2026 start, NSF–DOE Rubin Observatory formally began the 10-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time on June 30, 2026, kicking off nightly science-grade imaging of the southern sky roughly every 40 seconds.

events.title: Japanese Researchers and Engineers Confirmed as Key LSST Contributors
events.detail: As the Legacy Survey of Space and Time began full operations, NAOJ and Subaru Telescope confirmed Japan's ongoing role in LSST: NAOJ associate professor Yousuke Utsumi is stationed at Cerro Pachón as a Camera Operations Scientist applying Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam experience to LSST Camera optimization, while NAOJ, University of Tokyo, Chiba University, and Nagoya University researchers contribute data-management software and computing resources, and more than 80 Japanese researchers hold LSST data-access rights.

events.title: Early Data Preview 2 Delivers 3.2-Gigapixel COSMOS Mosaic
events.detail: Rubin released Early Data Preview 2 (EDP2) in early August 2026 — its first data preview built from full LSST Camera science observations — including a 3.2-gigapixel mosaic of the COSMOS field containing over 500,000 galaxies and 50,000 stars, with a second EDP2 phase of processed and difference images due in Q4 2026.

events.title: Founding Director Tony Tyson Named to TIME100
events.detail: Rubin Observatory founding director Tony Tyson, whose early-1990s survey-telescope concept helped originate the project, was named to the 2026 TIME100 list in recognition of the observatory's first year of results.
